As mentioned previously, the calcination conditions and template removal are important for pore formation, but the article neglected to report all of the conditions that are important for calcination, notably the ramp rate. Samples were subsequently prepared using ramp rates of 0.25- 1oC/min, different calcination gases, and an additional template extraction step prior to calcination. It was hypothesized that using N as the calcination gas would allow for some template to remain 2 in the structure and that performing another calcination step in air would remove the remaining template. The prepared samples were evaluated for their pore characteristics via N adsorption at 2 77 K. As indicated in Table 4, this proved to be true with sample MS8.1 showing the next highest pore volume of samples at 2.36 cm3/g followed by MS8 at 2.25 cm3/g. In addition, template extraction via methanol was explored as an option to controllably remove the template with an additional calcination step to ensure full template removal.
